item.research_question: What are the temperature-dependent mechanical properties and deformation mechanisms of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy additively manufactured by selective laser melting (SLM) compared to conventionally processed alloys?
item.processing_route: Selective laser melting (SLM) using pre-alloyed spherical powder (average diameter 27.2 µm); laser power 90 W, scan speed 600 mm/s, hatch space 80 µm, layer thickness 25 µm, volumetric energy density 75 J/mm³, 180° rotation scanning pattern, high-purity Ar atmosphere.
item.test_conditions: Compression tests at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C; initial strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹; engineering strain limit 0.4; specimens preheated at 10 °C/min; MoS₂ lubricant used.
key_findings: SLM-built HEA exhibited a yield strength of 778.4 MPa at room temperature, significantly higher than annealed (254.2 MPa) and other AM-processed (≈519 MPa) variants.
The alloy maintained superior mechanical properties up to 700 °C, with yield strength decreasing only slightly from 756.5 MPa at 25 °C to 545.8 MPa at 700 °C.
Average dislocation density was measured at 1.88 × 10¹⁴ m⁻², attributed to thermal contraction strain during rapid solidification.
Nano-sized Mn₂O₃ precipitates with an average size of 27.3 nm were identified at cell structure boundaries, with no Cr-Mn-based oxides or σ-phase formed.
Type-C serration occurred at 600 °C with a stress drop amplitude (Δσ) of ~4.5 MPa, associated with cooperative lattice diffusion (activation energy 335 kJ/mol).
Deformation mechanisms shifted from slip and deformation twinning (25–600 °C) to slip and partial dynamic recrystallization (700–900 °C).
Grain sizes varied by direction: 5.98 µm (building direction), 12.93 µm (transverse direction), and 15.66 µm (scanning direction).
Porosity was measured at 0.13%, with a density of 7.96 g/cm³.
item.mechanism: Superior mechanical properties at low temperatures (25–600 °C) are attributed to fine grain size, high dislocation density, and nano-sized Mn₂O₃ precipitates providing Orowan strengthening. At high temperatures (≥700 °C), dislocation forest hardening and Orowan strengthening remain dominant as matrix and grain boundary strengthening diminish. The delay in full recrystallization and strain softening up to 900 °C is caused by the Zener drag effect from Mn₂O₃ precipitates and migrated grain boundaries, which reduce the overall driving pressure for recrystallization.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that previous studies on AM-processed HEA were limited to fundamental investigations and room temperature properties.
item.future_work: The authors state that the study discusses correlations among microstructure, properties, and mechanisms but do not explicitly propose specific future work directions beyond the general implication that SLM allows for tuning alloys to be strong.
quotes: SLM-built HEA has a higher dislocation density of 1.88 × 10 14 m −2 as compared to the homogenized HEA.
